# Flow format reference

## Flow file format

An Ansible flow: a graph of typed nodes wired port to port. Hosts travel along the wires; every control port carries the hosts that took it. The designer edits this file; tools and AI assistants may write it too.

A flow is one YAML file named `<key>.flow.yaml`. The top level has one start node where the hosts enter; a subflow node has an inner level that its hosts enter through `subflow.boundary.in` and leave through exits (`boundary.outputs`). Hosts travel along the wires. Nodes are named by key; IDs (ULIDs) are added by tools. When you write YAML by hand, leave every `id:` out and use keys in wires and references, then run Complete IDs (flow_complete_ids, or the quick fix in the editor).

### Top level

- `schema_version` (1 | 2, required): Format version of this file: 2 for new flows; a 1 stays readable, and Upgrade Flow Format (or the upgrade_format op) moves it to 2 in one undo step.
- `flow` (object, required): The flow itself: identity, version, goal and the inputs a run asks for.
- `nodes` (list of node, required): Nodes of the top level, in any order. Subflow nodes hold their own inner level under subflow.
- `edges` (list of edge, required): Wires of the top level: an output port of one node to an input port of another node on the same level. One wire per output port.
- `layout` (layout): Canvas positions of every node at every level, by node ID (or by key while written by hand). Optional: missing positions are laid out automatically.
- `decisions` (list of object): Choices people made about the design: a fail port left open on purpose, a drift item or a lens finding kept as it is.

### flow

The flow itself: identity, version, goal and the inputs a run asks for.

- `id` (ulid): Fixed ID of the flow (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it. Never change it.
- `key` (slug, required): Short name of the flow: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Names the generated playbook.
- `name` (string, required): Human name of the flow.
- `version` (integer, required): Bumped once per commit when the design changes (not for layout moves). Tools bump it; do not edit by hand.
- `goal` (string): What the flow achieves, in a sentence.
- `owner` (string): Team or person that owns the flow.
- `runtime` (object): How the flow runs in AWX: a job template, or a workflow when approvals split it.
- `imported_from` (object): Where an imported flow came from, for reference only: a one-time copy
- `maintenance_window` (string): Longest time the flow may take, e.g. 4h or 2h30m (Timing lens)
- `inputs` (contract): Inputs a run asks for. A host_list input with targets: true seeds the hosts entering the start node.

### Node (nodes[], subflow.nodes[])

A step of the flow. Its type decides its ports; its status says how far it is built.

- `id` (ulid): Fixed ID of the node (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it. Never change it.
- `key` (slug, required): Short name, unique on its level: lowercase letters, digits and dashes. Wires and from: references may use it.
- `type` (start | end | task | subflow | decision | approval | parallel | join, required): start (one, on the top level; hosts enter), end (hosts leave; outcome success or failed), task, subflow (has an inner level), decision (true/false per host), approval (a person approves), parallel (branches), join (branches meet).
- `title` (string, required): Human name shown on the canvas.
- `intent` (string): What the node should do, in a sentence. Skeleton runs print it.
- `status` (draft | specified | implemented | tested): How far the node is built: draft (an idea), specified (has inputs or outputs), implemented (bound to code), tested (a passing run; set by runs only).
- `inputs` (contract): Values the node needs, usually from: an earlier node or a flow input.
- `outputs` (contract): Values the node produces for later nodes.
- `ports` (list of port): Optional ports enabled beyond the type defaults (e.g. unreachable, timeout, always on a task).
- `impl` (impl): What the node runs: a module, a role or a playbook. Absent: a TODO stub.
- `undo` (impl): What reverses the node, run by Rollback for the failed hosts.
- `condition` (string): Decision nodes: Jinja test without braces, evaluated per host; it reads the node's inputs
- `outcome` (success | failed): End nodes
- `join_mode` (all | any): Join nodes: per host, all = every branch delivered the host (default), any = at least one
- `branches` (integer): Parallel nodes: number of branch ports branch_1..branch_n (default 2)
- `handler` (rollback | notify | retry | exclude): Marks a failure handler node (what kind of handling it does)
- `settings` (object): How the node runs (play keywords).
- `subflow` (object): Subflow nodes: the inner level and how hosts enter and leave it.

### settings

How the node runs (play keywords).

- `max_fail_percentage` (number): Fail the whole node when more than this share of hosts fail.
- `serial` (string | integer): Batch size or percentage for rolling execution.
- `timeout` (string): Task timeout, e.g. 300 or 5m. Hosts that time out leave through the timeout port.
- `retries` (integer): Retries before a host fails (module steps). Without until, a step stops retrying on its first success.
- `delay` (integer): Seconds between retries (Ansible delay, default 5). retries x delay is how long a step polls.
- `until` (string): Poll until this holds: a Jinja test without braces, e.g. wait_ha_result.json.results | length == 2. It reads the step's registered result (impl.register, else <key with _ for ->_result) and its inputs. Module steps only; retries sets the attempts.
- `become` (boolean): Run with privilege escalation.
- `credential` (string): AWX credential name (AWX runs only).
- `execution_environment` (string): AWX execution environment name.
- `inventory_target` (string): Run the node's work on this host pattern instead of the arriving hosts (they leave together afterwards).
- `tags` (list of string): Extra Ansible tags for the generated play.

### subflow

Subflow nodes: the inner level and how hosts enter and leave it.

- `nodes` (list of node): Nodes of the inner level.
- `edges` (list of edge): Wires of the inner level.
- `layout` (layout): Old place for inner positions: read, never written (positions live in the top-level layout).
- `boundary` (object): How hosts enter and leave the subflow.

### subflow.boundary

How hosts enter and leave the subflow.

- `in` (nodeRef): The inner node that receives the hosts entering the subflow.
- `outputs` (map of list of exitref): Exits: a parent port name -> the inner outputs that leave through it.

### Wire (edges[])

A wire from an output port to an input port on the same level. Its hosts are the hosts that took that output.

- `id` (ulid): Fixed ID of the wire (ULID). Leave it out when writing by hand: Complete IDs adds it.
- `from` (portref, required): The output port the hosts leave from.
- `to` (portref, required): The input port they enter (usually in).

### Wire end (from, to)

One end of a wire: a node and one of its ports.

- `node` (nodeRef, required): The node: its ID, or its key while written by hand.
- `port` (string, required): Port name: an output (from) or an input (to) of that node.

### Subflow exit (boundary.outputs.<port>[])

An inner output that leaves the subflow.

- `node` (nodeRef, required): The inner node: its ID, or its key while written by hand.
- `port` (string, required): The inner node's output port.
- `reason` (string): Why hosts leave the subflow here (shown on the exit wire)

### Input or output field (inputs.<name>, outputs.<name>)

One input or output field.

- `type` (string | integer | boolean | list | dict | host_list | any, required): Value type. host_list is a list of inventory hosts or groups.
- `required` (boolean): Inputs: a run must provide a value.
- `default` (any): Inputs: value used when none is given.
- `from` (string): Where the value comes from: <node_key>.<output> (an earlier node's output, on this level or around it), flow.<input> (a flow input), <subflow_key>.<input> inside that subflow (its input), or impl.register[.path] (outputs: the bound task's registered result). A subflow's outputs name an inner step's output (<step>.<output>); without from, the inner output of the same name.
- `targets` (boolean): Flow inputs only: this host_list input seeds the start node's host set.

### Binding (impl, undo)

What the node runs: an Ansible module, a role or a playbook. null or absent: the node runs as a TODO stub (walking skeleton).

- `kind` (module | role | playbook, required): module, role or playbook.
- `ref` (string, required): Fully qualified module or role name (e.g. ansible.builtin.ping, netops.baseline), or the playbook path in the repository.
- `collection_version` (string): Collection version the binding was made against.
- `params` (object): Module parameters or role variables. Jinja may reference inputs by name.
- `register` (string): Variable that keeps the task result; outputs read it with from: impl.register.
- `keywords` (object): Ansible task keywords written on the generated task as they are (module and role bindings). Jinja may reference inputs by name; when, changed_when and failed_when are Jinja tests without braces. What the flow models itself is set there instead: register (impl.register), tags, become, timeout, retries, delay and until (settings), handlers (steps with when: <register> is changed), block and rescue (subflows and failure paths).

### Decision (decisions[])

One decision. kind decides which fields it needs.

- `node` (nodeRef): The node the decision is about (open_on_purpose, drift_ignored).
- `port` (string): open_on_purpose: the fail port left open on purpose.
- `kind` (open_on_purpose | drift_ignored | finding_accepted, required): open_on_purpose: a fail port stays unwired on purpose (hosts stop there); drift_ignored: design and code differ on purpose; finding_accepted: a lens finding is expected.
- `item` (string): drift_ignored: the drift item kept as it is
- `finding` (string): finding_accepted: the lens finding kept as expected
- `reason` (string): Why. Required in practice: the designer asks for it.
- `by` (string): Who decided (Git user name). Tools fill it in.

### A small flow written by hand

```yaml
schema_version: 2
flow:
  key: ntp-baseline
  name: NTP baseline
  version: 1
  inputs:
    devices: {type: host_list, required: true, targets: true}
nodes:
- {key: start, type: start, title: Start}
- {key: check-ntp, type: task, title: Check NTP, intent: Compare NTP servers with the standard}
- {key: done, type: end, title: Done, outcome: success}
edges:
- {from: {node: start, port: ok_hosts}, to: {node: check-ntp, port: in}}
- {from: {node: check-ntp, port: ok_hosts}, to: {node: done, port: in}}
decisions:
- {kind: open_on_purpose, node: check-ntp, port: failed_hosts, reason: Read-only check}
```

## Ports

Wires go from an output port to an input port (usually `in`) on the same level, one wire per output port. Optional ports must be enabled (enable_port) before they are wired. Parallel nodes have `branch_1..branch_n` (branches, default 2).

| Node type | Ports | Optional ports |
| --- | --- | --- |
| start | ok_hosts | - |
| end | in | - |
| task | in, ok_hosts, failed_hosts | unreachable, unchanged, always, cancelled, timeout, undo |
| subflow | in, ok_hosts, failed_hosts | unreachable, unchanged, always, cancelled, timeout, undo |
| decision | in, true, false | - |
| approval | in, approved, rejected | timeout |
| parallel | in, branch_1, branch_2 | - |
| join | in, ok_hosts | failed_hosts |

- `in` (input): hosts enter
- `ok_hosts` (output): hosts the step succeeded on
- `failed_hosts` (output): hosts it failed on
- `unreachable` (output): hosts that could not be reached
- `unchanged` (output): hosts it succeeded on without changing anything
- `always` (output): every host after the step, whatever the outcome
- `cancelled` (output): hosts of a cancelled run (Run mode only)
- `timeout` (output): hosts that ran out of time (settings.timeout; approvals: no answer in time)
- `undo` (input): Rollback runs the undo binding for these hosts
- `true` (output): hosts the condition is true for
- `false` (output): hosts it is false for
- `approved` (output): hosts a person approved
- `rejected` (output): hosts a person rejected
- `branch_<n>` (output): every host, once per branch (parallel)

Fail ports (failed_hosts, unreachable, timeout, rejected) must be handled: wired (often with apply_pattern), or left open on purpose with a reason (leave_open). Unhandled fail ports are warnings; their hosts fail the run.

## Failure patterns (apply_pattern)

| Pattern | What it adds | Fits ports | Node types |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| rollback | Rollback from Backup: Undo the completed nodes for the failed hosts only (reuses the Rollback of this level) | failed_hosts | any |
| notify-stop | Notify On-Call and Stop: Open a ticket, page on-call, end these hosts as stopped | failed_hosts, unreachable, timeout, rejected | any |
| retry | Retry with Backoff: Run the step again for these hosts, then rejoin the happy path | failed_hosts, unreachable, timeout | task, subflow |
| exclude | Exclude and Report: Take these hosts out of the run and list them in the report | failed_hosts, unreachable | any |
| stop | Stop Flow: End these hosts with a failed outcome | failed_hosts, unreachable, timeout, rejected | any |
| done | Connect to Done: End these hosts with a success outcome | ok_hosts, unchanged, approved, true, false | any |
| escalate | Escalate Approval: Ask the next approver; approved hosts rejoin the happy path | rejected, timeout | approval |
| report | Send Run Report: Send per-host results after the step, whatever the outcome | always | any |
